claims: Colon cancer symptoms include changes in bowel habits such as constipation, diarrhea, or narrowing of the stool that lasts for more than a few weeks.
Colon cancer symptoms include rectal bleeding such as blood in the stool that is dark or bright red or on toilet paper.
Colon cancer symptoms include abdominal discomfort such as persistent cramps, pain, gas, bloating, or a feeling that the bowel does not empty completely.
Colon cancer symptoms include systemic issues such as unexplained weight loss, weakness, fatigue, and iron deficiency anemia.
Colon cancer symptoms include a constant need to have a bowel movement when none is passed.
Many people with colon cancer have no symptoms at first.
Symptoms associated with colon cancer can also be caused by non-cancerous conditions such as infections, hemorrhoids, or inflammatory bowel disease (IBD).
